headline: Fixes from a fourth review
change: Pasting a listing starts clean: no bungalow, council tax band, size, price or rent carries over from the last paste.

headline: Fixes from a fourth review
change: Listings: the type is read correctly past 'flat roof', 'roof terrace' and 'detached garage'; bedrooms can be words; the agent's postcode is ignored; street chips are whole postcodes; a listing with no location no longer values the last postcode.

headline: Fixes from a fourth review
change: Investing: a price, rent or EPC cost you type stays when you edit the same home's details, and resets for a different home.

headline: Fixes from a fourth review
change: The flip calculator uses your purchase price, finances part of it as a bridging loan, and gives the highest price that breaks even or makes a 15% margin.

headline: Fixes from a fourth review
change: The 10-year IRR is after tax on the gain (capital gains tax, or corporation tax for a company), and corporation tax has marginal relief.

headline: Fixes from a fourth review
change: The 'matches the gilt' rent allows for the risk allowance; a £0 rent scores as the lowest yield; the projection uses the scorecard's growth figure.

headline: Fixes from a fourth review
change: Decorating a home that needs a full renovation no longer counts as making it 'good'.

headline: Fixes from a fourth review
change: Postcodes outside Doncaster are refused; DN11 and DN12 searches find those districts; no more '−0.0' figures; typing redraws once you pause.

headline: Fixes from a fourth review
change: Condition setting recalibrated (folds grouped by home, long-hold resale uplift removed): −8.9% for needs full renovation, +6.2% for recently refurbished.

headline: Fixes from a fourth review
change: Accuracy tab: a fair hedonic baseline on the same features (9.8%), accuracy by sale year and for new builds, and the registration lag explained.

headline: Fixes from a fourth review
change: The public copy no longer shows house names; the 10-year gilt is updated to 5.48%.

headline: Fixes from a third review
change: An impossible price, rent or running cost now clears the investment scorecard until it is fixed. A £500 price used to show a 1,536% return.

headline: Fixes from a third review
change: A cleared figure can no longer be written back by a count-up still running, and the 'Use this rent' button goes when there is no estimate.

headline: Fixes from a third review
change: The IRR finds repeated and very close rates. When the cash flows change sign more than once, it warns that the IRR can mislead and gives the NPV.

headline: Fixes from a third review
change: Each panel checks only the inputs it uses: an impossible deposit clears the mortgage results but not the cash scorecard, and the flip appraisal refuses impossible months, finance rates and bathrooms.

headline: Fixes from a third review
change: New tests change inputs during animations and while typing, not only on settled screens.

headline: Fixes from a second review
change: A pasted listing no longer loses details that match the selected certificate: each field now records whether a certificate, a listing or you filled it.

headline: Fixes from a second review
change: An impossible input clears everything from the last estimate: asking-price advice, explanation, comparables, what-if, and the Investing scorecard and rent.

headline: Fixes from a second review
change: The IRR finds every rate that fits; when there are two or more it says the IRR is ambiguous and gives the NPV at the 10-year gilt.

headline: Fixes from a second review
change: The strict timing check runs three seeds, and its wording is plainer: little aggregate change, and a sensitivity test rather than a bound.

headline: Fixes from a second review
change: Unit and browser regression tests ship with the project.

headline: Fixes from an independent review
change: The model on this page is refitted on every kept sale to August 2025; sales from January to August 2025 had been left out by mistake.

headline: Fixes from an independent review
change: Landlord tax: the Section 24 credit is capped at the property profit, and unused interest and losses carry forward through the projection.

headline: Fixes from an independent review
change: Choosing another address, or clearing it, no longer keeps the previous home's size and rooms.

headline: Fixes from an independent review
change: Impossible inputs, such as a negative floor area or a 150% deposit, are refused and the old results cleared.

headline: Fixes from an independent review
change: The IRR handles returns above 150% and says when no rate fits or more than one may.

headline: Fixes from an independent review
change: Flood allowance corrected: a typical let falls outside Flood Re, so the scenario is £445 a year, to check with a quote.

headline: Fixes from an independent review
change: A strict timing check and accuracy for homes typed in by hand on the Model accuracy tab; the rent model's error is now a share of the actual rent.

headline: Version number and changelog
change: The header shows the version and its date; click it to open this tab.

headline: Version number and changelog
change: A Changelog tab lists every version, newest first.

headline: Easier period picking on the price time-lapse
change: A two-handle period slider and quick buttons (since 1995, since 2000, 20, 10 or 5 years, 2007 to 2013) that work on a phone.

headline: Easier period picking on the price time-lapse
change: Doncaster's line stays whole, with the chosen period shaded; dragging across it still works with a mouse.

headline: Growth over a chosen period, and the risk allowance on
change: Prices since 1995: the map shows each neighbourhood's growth over a chosen period against Doncaster's, with each year's change one click away.

headline: Growth over a chosen period, and the risk allowance on
change: The risk allowance starts switched on.

headline: Growth over a chosen period, and the risk allowance on
change: Flood insurance allowance cut from £600 to £110 a year, from Flood Re's figures; buy-to-let owned by individuals qualifies for Flood Re.

headline: Growth over a chosen period, and the risk allowance on
change: Tenancies ending in court moved to the bottom of the Market tab.

headline: Refurbishment costs that scale sensibly
change: A kitchen and a rewire grow with the square root of floor area; bathrooms and the boiler are fixed amounts.

headline: Refurbishment costs that scale sensibly
change: The guides' 3-bed prices apply at Doncaster's typical 3-bed semi (84 m²), which lowers the per-m² trades by about 14%.

headline: Refurbishment costs that scale sensibly
change: Kitchen and bathroom finish follows the home's value unless one is chosen.

headline: Refurbishment costs that scale sensibly
change: The contingency is an input on the page.

headline: Sourced refurbishment costs
change: Unsourced per-m² guesses, which ran 3 to 6 times too high, replaced with Yorkshire guide prices item by item and a 10% contingency.

headline: Sourced refurbishment costs
change: Kitchens and bathrooms priced per room rather than per m² of the whole home.

headline: Sourced refurbishment costs
change: Buy, refurbish and sell buys at the condition the works put right; VAT and your own quote can be added.

headline: Risk allowance
change: A switch takes allowances for tenant risk, flood insurance, energy rules and a future downturn off area and property returns.

headline: Tenant risk
change: Landlord court claims (Ministry of Justice) on the Market tab, and anti-social behaviour (police.uk) by neighbourhood.

headline: Tenant risk
change: Comparisons with the neighbourhood in percentages instead of standard deviations.

headline: Tenant risk
change: A minimum price filter for the best buy-to-let list.

headline: Tenant risk
change: The time-lapse no longer plays by itself.

headline: Tenant risk
change: The Invest tab renamed Investing.

headline: Investing tab
change: A home against recent sales in its neighbourhood: price against value, price per m² and yield.

headline: Investing tab
change: A rent estimate linked to value, with its likely range.

headline: Investing tab
change: The opportunity-cost buttons show each rate and its source on hover.

headline: Investing tab
change: Sales history fixed for streets that share a name in different places.

headline: Investing tab
change: "Habitable rooms" renamed "bedrooms and living rooms".

headline: Neighbourhoods, motion and dark mode
change: 39 named neighbourhoods with repeat-sales growth since 1995, yields, total return and return above an opportunity cost.

headline: Neighbourhoods, motion and dark mode
change: A best buy-to-let ranking, a neighbourhood search, and map colours red for worse and blue for better.

headline: Neighbourhoods, motion and dark mode
change: The Prices since 1995 time-lapse and other motion.

headline: Neighbourhoods, motion and dark mode
change: A light and dark switch.

headline: Testing and confidence
change: A year-by-year backtest since 2020.

headline: Testing and confidence
change: Confidence levels, with 80% ranges that follow them.

headline: Testing and confidence
change: The assessors' ratio study and a Model accuracy tab.

headline: Full-size model in the browser
change: All 2,043 trees run in the page.

headline: Full-size model in the browser
change: Energy-certificate history added: median error 8.03%.

headline: Full-size model in the browser
change: A comparison with simple valuation methods.

headline: What-ifs and sales history
change: What would works add: extensions, lofts and energy upgrades against sourced costs.

headline: What-ifs and sales history
change: Sales history since 1995 for a picked address.

headline: What-ifs and sales history
change: A prompt for homes that may have been extended.

headline: More about the home
change: Plot size from title plans, street and postcode prices, and more certificate detail; tuned settings.

headline: More about the home
change: A SHAP breakdown of each estimate, a council tax band check and a Saved list.

headline: Local correction
change: Each estimate shifted by half the median miss on the 40 nearest recent sales, cutting the spread of area bias from 2.3% to 1.5%.

headline: More data, tested first
change: Flood risk, transport, schools and amenities tested in the model, and shown for each home instead.

headline: More data, tested first
change: A neighbourhood map on 2021 small areas.

headline: Energy certificates and last sale
change: Certificates matched to sales by address; nearest-sale and last-sale inputs took the median error from 13.2% to 8.6%.

headline: Energy certificates and last sale
change: Paste a listing, look up an address, and buy-to-let tax by owner type.

headline: First model and dashboard
change: LightGBM against a ridge baseline on a time-based split, with a quality-adjusted price index.

headline: First model and dashboard
change: Checked 80% ranges, a condition setting calibrated on quick resales, and buy-to-let numbers.

headline: Fixes from a fifth review
change: Capital gains tax for a basic-rate owner: 18% only on the part of the gain that fits in the unused basic-rate band, after your other income (£20,000 unless you enter it) and that year's rental profit; 24% on the rest.

headline: Fixes from a fifth review
change: Only improvements come off the gain. Repairs and decorating (the rest of the works and EPC upgrade) are deducted from the first year's rental profit instead.

headline: Fixes from a fifth review
change: A listing that names only a district (Doncaster DN4) no longer keeps the last home's postcode; a dashed chip offers to keep it.

headline: Fixes from a fifth review
change: The flip calculator no longer swaps your figures: an invalid price clears it, a blank price uses the model value, and a £0 works quote stays £0.

headline: Fixes from a fifth review
change: Condition setting by what the model knows: with a last sale on record, needs full renovation is −4.7% and a resale within 18 months of it +0.6%, against −8.9% and +6.2% without one.

headline: Fixes from a fifth review
change: Build: the page source lives in dashboard/ and every assumption in config/assumptions.csv; a test rebuilds the public copy from the zip byte for byte.

headline: Fixes from a fifth review
change: The Market and Accuracy tabs are drawn by a script of their own (one page file can't exceed 256 KB).

headline: Three new views of a deal
change: Mortgage rate chart: the first year's monthly cash flow, before and after tax, at every rate, with the break-even rate and where the lender's stress test fails. Drag the slider or across the chart and the whole deal follows.

headline: Three new views of a deal
change: What matters most: a tornado of the 10-year IRR after tax, or the first year's cash flow, with each input lowered and raised by a set amount (price paid, rent, rate, growth, voids, maintenance, deposit). The bars move as you edit the deal.

headline: Three new views of a deal
change: If prices follow a past decade: the deal's equity over 10 years if the price had followed the neighbourhood's prices after each purchase year since 1995, with each year's after-tax IRR against the 10-year gilt.

headline: Three new views of a deal
change: The deal's 10-year projection is worked out in one place, so the tiles, the projection and the three new charts always agree.

headline: Current mortgage rate
change: The default mortgage rate is 5.66%, Moneyfacts' average 5-year fixed buy-to-let rate at 75% loan to value (1 August 2026), up from June 2025's 5.29%. Rates have risen since, so enter a current quote.

headline: Ready to publish
change: Licence and attribution notes for every data source, in the footer and the README; d3's licence ships with the page; the shared copy keeps comparable sales to street and postcode.

headline: Labels that fit on a phone
change: On a phone, the rent estimate's labels (housing benefit cap, the break-even and gilt-matching rents and the others) no longer print over each other: each takes the first row where it fits, and the chart grows when it needs more rows.

headline: Labels that fit on a phone
change: The 'Prices since 1995' line labels its boom, peak, low and recovery in fewer words on a narrow screen, and leaves out a label that would overlap another (its dot stays).

headline: Labels that fit on a phone
change: Rebuilding the public copy on Windows gives the same file as anywhere else: d3 is read as UTF-8, so its minus sign and µ come through, and lines end the same way.
